domain: Space science, fundamental physics and exotic-propulsion ceilings

bottlenecks.name: Forward models of the sources
bottlenecks.description: Predicting what an instrument should see: gravitational waveforms (numerical relativity, gravitational self-force), exoplanet atmosphere and molecular-opacity models, coronal and solar-wind models, cosmological simulations. Errors here become biased science: LISA studies show neglected higher harmonics or eccentricity bias massive-black-hole parameters at SNRs in the hundreds to thousands, and JWST retrievals of the same spectrum give disparate answers.
bottlenecks.share_of_effort: ~30% of modeling and analysis effort in the domain (analyst judgment)
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: High where the work is expert-scarce derivation plus code: second-order self-force on spinning black holes, well-posedness of beyond-Einstein gravity, error-controlled waveform surrogates. Under S2 these 5-8 year programs could compress to 2-3 years. Low where lab data or compute binds: opacities need laboratory spectroscopy, LISA-grade numerical relativity needs supercomputer time.

bottlenecks.name: Inverse problems and inference at scale
bottlenecks.description: Turning data into parameters with honest uncertainty: LISA's 'global fit' of tens of thousands of overlapping signals, exoplanet atmospheric retrievals, simulation-based cosmological inference for DESI, Euclid, Rubin and Roman, sparse-aperture VLBI imaging (EHT, BHEX), 3D heliospheric tomography from a few viewpoints (PUNCH).
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: High and fast: identifiability and stability theorems (what a dataset can and cannot determine), calibrated inference with coverage guarantees, certified emulators. Mostly P3/P5 within 1-3 years with no hardware needed; collaboration adoption is the gate. Mostly 'solved in principle but expert-scarce' rather than famous open problems.

bottlenecks.name: Instrument stability and integrated modeling
bottlenecks.description: Closing error budgets for extreme instruments: HWO needs raw contrast ~1e-10, 1-sigma photometric precision ~3e-12 and contrast drift of order 1e-11 to 1e-10 during observations, which means picometer-class wavefront stability; LISA needs drag-free control and picometer interferometry; space clocks and atom interferometers need full systematic-error models.
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Medium: provable coronagraph throughput limits, wavefront controllers with convergence and robustness guarantees, AI-run integrated structural-thermal-optical models. But testbeds, deformable mirrors, detectors and thermal hardware set achieved performance, and testbed time is scarce.

bottlenecks.name: Data supply: photons, missions, downlink and lab measurements
bottlenecks.description: Most open science questions in the domain (is dark energy evolving, is a gas biological, why is the corona hot) are data-limited. Mission count is set by budgets: NASA's FY2026 budget is $24.4B and the FY2027 request is $18.8B. Laboratory opacities and reaction rates are a separate, slow data supply.
bottlenecks.share_of_effort: ~15% of effort, but the dominant binding constraint
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Low: optimal experimental design and better target selection squeeze more from each photon but cannot create data. Autonomous labs (S2/S3) can speed laboratory spectroscopy and chemical kinetics.

bottlenecks.name: Credibility of extraordinary claims
bottlenecks.description: Checking biosignature detections (the K2-18 b dimethyl-sulfide debate), dark-energy anomalies, new-physics hints and exotic-propulsion proposals. Today small groups do this over months to years: Lentz's 2020 positive-energy warp claim was shown to violate the weak energy condition only in Nov 2025.
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: High and fast (P3): independent AI re-analysis within weeks; certified checks (interval-arithmetic energy-condition tests for warp metrics already exist). Limits: reviewer attention and formal libraries; Mathlib has essentially no Lorentzian geometry, so GR claims cannot yet be Lean-checked (general).

bottlenecks.name: Programmatics: flagship schedules and budgets
bottlenecks.description: LISA launches in 2035; HWO in the 2040s; small missions need competitive selection (BHEX plans a 2026 Small Explorer proposal and a 2031 launch). These dates set when any math-enabled capability can fly.
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Nil on dates. Indirect only: cheaper design closure and stronger proposals.

nodes.title: Black-hole foundations settled and checked
nodes.description: Independent experts confirm the 2026 wave of mathematical general relativity: nonlinear stability of Kerr black holes across the full subextremal range (human preprints, Jun and Sep 2026), the AI-claimed strong cosmic censorship near Kerr (family 264) and the AI-claimed spacetime Penrose inequalities (family 260). Together they make 'perturbed black holes settle down to Kerr, and their mass bounds their horizon area' a theorem rather than an assumption.
nodes.status_oct2026: Kerr stability in the full subextremal range claimed by Hintz (arXiv 2606.28253, Jun 2026) and Szeftel (arXiv 2609.40068, Sep 2026), human work, not yet refereed. Family 264 (strong cosmic censorship near two-ended Kerr data): T1, manuscript only. Family 260 (spacetime Penrose inequalities): T1 for the main inequalities; only a supporting construction (Cha-Khuri-Sakovich end replacement, Comparator target CKSBondiPenrose) has an agent-written Lean proof, unchecked, and the repo's lean/docs/260.md states the paper's general inequality 'remains unformalized'. Neither family appears in formalization.yaml as a formalized main result.
nodes.premise_tier: T1 (families 260 main results and 264); human Kerr-stability preprints unrefereed
nodes.why: Ringdown spectroscopy (LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA now, LISA after 2035) and EHT/BHEX photon-ring tests all assume a perturbed black hole relaxes to Kerr. Kerr stability proves it from outside; strong cosmic censorship near Kerr (264) says the interior generically cannot be continued past the Cauchy horizon with square-integrable connection; Penrose inequalities (260) bound mass below by horizon area for moving, charged and rotating data. Review bandwidth is the gate: a few dozen people can referee these, and 722 manuscripts arrived at once (tr-position-5). Formal checking is further off because Lean lacks Lorentzian geometry, so S1 is Medium; S2/S3 add AI-assisted refereeing and formalization.
nodes.strongest_case_small: No working astrophysicist doubted the Kerr final state. Waveform models, ringdown tests and EHT analyses already assume it, so nothing in any instrument or mission changes; this removes a theoretical doubt only (tl-position-2).
nodes.signpost: A named GR expert publicly endorses or finds a gap in families 260 or 264 by end-2027; Hintz or Szeftel accepted by a journal; first Lean library for Lorentzian causal structure.

nodes.title: Warp drives: sharp no-go theorems
nodes.description: Theorems stating, for every metric in a broad class, how much negative energy a 'warp' or 'propellantless' spacetime needs, or how much positive mass a positive-energy version must carry. Superluminal bubbles must violate the null energy condition; positive-energy subluminal shells must carry planetary-scale mass; the sharp constants are now being computed.
nodes.status_oct2026: Human literature, mostly T5: generic warp drives violate the null energy condition (arXiv 2105.03079, 2021); a subluminal warp satisfies all energy conditions only by adding a matter shell with positive ADM mass (arXiv 2405.02709, 2024); Lentz's positive-energy claim refuted (arXiv 2511.18251, Nov 2025); new no-go theorems and classification (arXiv 2602.16495, Feb 2026); exact minimum Eulerian negative energy for Natario drives, E_min ~ v^2 R^4/(4 Delta^3) (arXiv 2609.36211, Sep 28 2026). The spacetime positive mass theorem (zero ADM mass with dominant energy forces flat spacetime) is established. Family 260 (T1) extends Penrose mass-area bounds to data with arbitrary momentum, a marginal addition.
nodes.premise_tier: T5 for the null-energy and positive-mass results; T1 for the family 260 extension (not load-bearing)
nodes.why: Ceilings act within months (fc-position-1). The numbers are brutal: (1) by the Natario result, halving the bubble wall thickness multiplies the negative energy needed 8x and doubling the bubble radius multiplies it 16x; for R/Delta = 100 the sharp bound is 2,500x the older v^2R^2/Delta estimate. (2) A positive-energy configuration that contains a trapped surface of enclosing radius 10 m must have ADM mass >= r/2 in geometric units, about 6.7e27 kg or 3.5 Jupiter masses (family 260 for moving data, conditional on T1). (3) Any 'zero-mass' warp metric that is not flat must violate the dominant energy condition (positive mass rigidity). An exponentially improving model can extend these to every published warp class with sharp constants, which is cognitive work only.
nodes.strongest_case_small: The answer was already 'no' before AI: the null-energy result dates from 2021 and positive mass from 1979-81. Family 260 applies only to energy-respecting data with trapped surfaces, which typical subluminal warp shells lack, so the catalog adds almost nothing to propulsion. Nothing that could fly is removed.
nodes.signpost: An AI-produced general theorem covering all published warp classes (Alcubierre, Natario, Lentz, Bobrick-Martire, Fell-Heisenberg, Fuchs et al.) with interval-certified or formal checks; or a credible counterexample class that survives audit.

nodes.title: Hard limits on negative energy from quantum fields
nodes.description: Quantum energy inequalities cap how much negative energy any quantum field can hold and for how long. They are proven for free fields in flat space and some curved backgrounds; general curved spacetimes and interacting fields remain open. Settling them would close the 'quantum loophole' (Casimir-type sources) that warp and wormhole proposals rely on.
nodes.status_oct2026: (general) Ford-Roman and Fewster quantum inequalities established for free fields; averaged null energy condition proven for flat-space QFT (2016-17); interacting and generic curved cases open. Not in the catalog.
nodes.why: Exotic-propulsion proposals concede classical matter cannot supply negative energy and point to quantum effects. A general quantum inequality would bound the product of negative-energy magnitude and duration for any physical source, completing the ceiling started by the classical theorems. Under S2 research-grade mathematical physics is routine by 2028-29, so partial-to-general results by 2029 are plausible.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Interacting four-dimensional quantum field theories are not rigorously constructed, so the fully general theorem may not even be statable; and the classical no-go results already exclude every macroscopic proposal at absurd energy scales.
nodes.signpost: A proven quantum energy inequality for a nontrivial interacting model or for general globally hyperbolic backgrounds, with AI credited.

nodes.title: Beyond-Einstein gravity made simulable
nodes.description: Proving which modified-gravity theories have a well-posed initial-value problem, so black-hole mergers can be simulated and turned into templates, or proving they do not. Without it, gravitational-wave tests of general relativity rely on parametrized, theory-agnostic deviations.
nodes.status_oct2026: Well-posedness shown for Horndeski and Einstein-scalar-Gauss-Bonnet at weak coupling in modified harmonic gauge (Kovacs-Reall 2020, general); puncture-gauge formulation for four-derivative scalar-tensor theories (Phys. Rev. D, Oct 2023); first fully nonlinear Einstein-scalar-Gauss-Bonnet scattering simulations (arXiv 2605.04224, May 2026). Dynamical Chern-Simons and strong coupling open, usually handled by order-reduction schemes without proofs. No catalog family.
nodes.why: A well-posedness proof lets numerical-relativity groups produce merger waveforms in a specific alternative theory, so LISA (2035+) and ground detectors can test that theory directly. A negative result is just as useful (tl-position-2): it marks theories that can only be treated as effective field theories, telling analysts which tests are meaningful. Pure PDE analysis, exactly the S2 2027-28 capability.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Most strong-field tests already use parametrized deviations, general relativity has passed every test so far, and LISA does not fly until 2035, so the payoff is mostly bounds on theories rather than a discovery.
nodes.signpost: Proof or disproof of strong hyperbolicity for dynamical Chern-Simons beyond weak coupling; NR codes adopting proven formulations.

nodes.title: LISA's hardest waveforms: second-order self-force around spinning black holes
nodes.description: Extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (a stellar-mass black hole spiraling ~1e5 orbits into a massive one) can only be decoded if the phase is modeled to better than about a radian over the whole signal. That requires second-order gravitational self-force for generic (eccentric, inclined) orbits around spinning Kerr black holes.
nodes.status_oct2026: Second-order calculations exist only for quasicircular orbits around non-spinning (Schwarzschild) black holes (arXiv 2112.12265; effective-source paper arXiv 2508.00087, 2025); a June 2026 paper states 'these calculations have only been attempted for the simplest case of circular orbits in Schwarzschild spacetime' and demonstrates a numerical-relativity route in Kerr for a scalar charge (arXiv 2606.04998); Lorenz-gauge elliptic methods in progress (arXiv 2608.07934, Aug 2026). Adiabatic-order Kerr waveforms for equatorial orbits exist in the FastEMRIWaveforms framework (Phys. Rev. D, Apr 2025); interpolation errors in such fast models are themselves a bias source (PRD, Mar 2026).
nodes.why: The phase expands as phi = phi_0/epsilon + phi_1 + O(epsilon) with mass ratio epsilon ~1e-5 to 1e-6; adiabatic waveforms carry only phi_0, and the O(1) post-adiabatic term phi_1 needs second-order self-force (general). The formalism exists; what is missing is expert labor: renormalized second-order sources, gauge transformations, mode coupling and eccentric/inclined Kerr orbits, by a field of a few dozen specialists. This is the 'solved in principle, expert-scarce' class where on-demand AI applied math (P1) acts first. Under S2 it lands ~2029, four to six years ahead of a pre-AI path that aimed only to finish before the 2035 launch.
nodes.strongest_case_small: LISA's science date is fixed by its 2035 launch, so finishing early buys risk reduction, not earlier science; and offline-online surrogates still need validation against independent codes.
nodes.signpost: First second-order self-force results for eccentric orbits or a Kerr background by 2028, with AI credited in methods or authorship.

nodes.title: Merger simulations precise enough for LISA's loudest signals
nodes.description: LISA will see massive black-hole mergers at signal-to-noise ratios in the hundreds to thousands, where waveform error dominates the error budget. Simulations need mismatches near 1e-6 (indistinguishability scales as ~1/(2 SNR^2), general) at mass ratios above 10 and spins near 0.9, versus ~1e-4 typical today.
nodes.status_oct2026: SXS third catalog (CQG, Aug 2025): 3,756 configurations, precessing up to mass ratio 8 and spins <= 0.8. Typical resolution mismatch ~1e-4, but ~1e-1 for the longest (~180-orbit) runs (arXiv 2502.14025). Bias studies show neglected harmonics and eccentricity bias LISA parameters (arXiv 2502.12237, 2602.09088, 2601.07739). GPU code generation for NR emerging (arXiv 2501.14030).
nodes.why: A 100x accuracy gain at extreme parameters requires better formulations, a-posteriori error estimators, high-order discontinuous-Galerkin codes and GPU ports (cognitive, compresses under S2), then very large supercomputer allocations (capital, does not compress). That is why S3 is no better than Medium: compute time binds even when cognition is free.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Accuracy can also be bought by hybridizing NR with self-force and effective-one-body models, which the field already does; AI mostly speeds code work, and the 2035 launch sets the deadline.
nodes.signpost: A public catalog with precessing runs at mass ratio >= 16 and mismatch <= 1e-5; NR codes shipping certified error estimates.

nodes.title: LISA analysis stack passes its accuracy tests
nodes.description: End-to-end validation in LISA mock-data challenges: waveform models (post-adiabatic self-force inspirals, NR-calibrated mergers) plus the 'global fit' that separates tens of thousands of overlapping signals, shown to recover injected parameters without bias at realistic signal strengths. The ground-test analog for a science instrument.
nodes.status_oct2026: LISA adopted by ESA in Jan 2024 (general); construction began Jun 17 2025; launch planned 2035 (ESA). Global-fit and source-separation methods under active development (e.g., arXiv 2606.01236, May 2026).
nodes.why: Readiness requires both waveform families plus validation within the consortium's data-challenge cadence and acceptance process (adoption gate). Under S2 the theory inputs land 2029-30, so readiness is credible by 2030; under S1 the self-force input is not done by 2031.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Being ready in 2030 rather than 2033 changes nothing observable before the 2035 launch; the gain is lower schedule risk for the science ground segment.
nodes.signpost: LISA data-challenge results with post-adiabatic EMRI injections recovered without bias.

nodes.title: LISA does precision strong-gravity science from day one
nodes.description: When LISA flies, its first-year data yield unbiased black-hole masses and spins, extreme-mass-ratio tests of the Kerr metric and bounds on beyond-Einstein theories, because the theory work was finished years before launch instead of during operations.
nodes.status_oct2026: Launch planned 2035 on Ariane 6 (ESA).
nodes.why: Shown to make the physical clock visible: AI mathematics can move LISA's theory readiness forward by four to six years under S2, but the science cannot begin before the spacecraft fly in 2035.
nodes.strongest_case_small: By construction nothing happens before 2031.
nodes.signpost: ESA LISA milestones (critical design review, launch date) hold or slip; no AI scenario moves them.

nodes.title: Exoplanet atmosphere readings with honest error bars
nodes.description: Theorems and certified tools stating which molecules, abundances and temperature structures a given spectrum can and cannot determine (identifiability), plus retrieval methods robust to wrong one-dimensional model assumptions. Turns today's 'parallel interpretations' into quantified, comparable claims.
nodes.status_oct2026: JWST shows 'established inverse methods ... can lead to disparate interpretations even with JWST's quality of data' (Seager et al., PNAS, Sep 2025). The K2-18 b DMS signal remains disputed (homogeneous MIRI survey, ApJL Sep 2026; 661-molecule agnostic search, ApJL May 2026; Hycean vs mini-Neptune debate, arXiv 2605.17803). No general identifiability theory for retrieval forward models (general).
nodes.why: Identifiability maps tell observers which wavelength range, resolution and SNR make a molecule recoverable; robust inference stops 1D-model misspecification from producing false detections. That shortens claim-and-rebuttal cycles from months to weeks and feeds HWO's wavelength and resolution requirements. Pure applied mathematics and statistics; the gate is community adoption.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Degeneracies are physics, not math: if the spectrum lacks the information, no theorem creates it. JWST's noise floor, stellar contamination and opacity errors are the real limits.
nodes.signpost: A community retrieval comparison (K2-18 b, TRAPPIST-1 planets) reporting AI-derived identifiability maps; journals asking for identifiability statements.

nodes.title: Molecular fingerprints good enough for biosignature claims
nodes.description: Accurate line lists, pressure broadening and collision-induced absorption for biosignature and false-positive molecules (DMS, DMDS, CH3Cl, N2O, PH3, O2-O2 and others) over the needed temperatures, computed by AI-driven quantum chemistry and validated in the laboratory.
nodes.status_oct2026: Opacity data of uneven quality underlie broad molecule searches (661 species tested for K2-18 b, ApJL May 2026); incomplete opacities are a known retrieval systematic (general). Catalog 275 (QMA-hardness of continuum Coulomb energy, T1) and 278 (failure of Kohn-Sham ensemble representability, T1) are worst-case ceilings on general electronic-structure methods, not obstacles for small molecules.
nodes.premise_tier: n/a (catalog families enter only as ceilings, conditional on T1)
nodes.why: Ab initio line-list production is labor-heavy and expert-scarce; AI theory compresses it, and autonomous spectroscopy labs (S2/S3) validate faster. Lab validation stays the slowest link, so even S3 is only Medium. The hardness results (275, 278) say no general algorithm exists, which reinforces the need for lab checks rather than blocking progress.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Line-list production is already a mature pipeline (ExoMol, HITRAN); lab spectroscopy capacity, not theory, limits validation.
nodes.signpost: Database releases with AI-computed line lists validated against lab spectra for 50+ new species.

nodes.title: Knowing when 'signs of life' are not life
nodes.description: Predictive photochemistry, geochemistry and 3D climate models that list the non-biological routes to O2, O3, CH4 with CO2, DMS and other biosignatures for a given star and planet, with probabilities attached. This is the theory HWO needs to turn a detection into a claim.
nodes.status_oct2026: JWST results push the field to 'parallel interpretations' that may not be resolved until the next generation of observatories (PNAS, Sep 2025); 1D retrievals are 'highly averaged' representations of 3D processes (same).
nodes.why: Under S2 AI builds physics theory by 2028-29 and autonomous labs supply rate constants, so a quantified false-positive map is credible by 2030. Mission-design effect: it decides whether HWO needs ultraviolet (O3), near-infrared to ~1.8 microns (CH4, CO2) or both, which drives coronagraph and detector choices.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Planetary context (interior, history, surface) is underdetermined by remote data; even perfect theory yields a probability, not a verdict.
nodes.signpost: HWO science-requirements documents cite AI-generated false-positive maps; autonomous photochemistry labs publishing rate constants at scale.

nodes.title: Proven limits for starlight suppression
nodes.description: Sharp, provable bounds on how much planet light any coronagraph can deliver at a given inner working angle, bandwidth and 1e-10 contrast for HWO's candidate apertures (on-axis segmented versus off-axis), plus designs that approach them. Shows which architectures cannot meet the 25-exo-Earth goal before money is spent.
nodes.status_oct2026: HWO needs raw contrast ~1e-10 and 1-sigma photometric precision ~3e-12 (arXiv 2510.02547, Oct 2025); vortex and forked-grating designs under study (JATIS, Sep 2026); coronagraph design is already posed as optimization with electric-field conjugation (JATIS 2022); an analytic error budget from optical disturbances to flux-ratio noise appeared Sep 2026 (arXiv 2609.32023). Ideal-coronagraph limits exist only for idealized apertures (general).
nodes.why: Coronagraph design reduces to optimization over linear optical operators, where convex duality yields provable upper bounds (a ceiling, P3) and the primal solution yields designs (P4, if manufacturable). Architecture down-select for HWO happens over roughly 2027-30, so a ceiling that arrives in 2027-28 can prune options while it still matters.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Achieved contrast is set by mask fabrication tolerances, polarization aberrations, detector noise and stability, not by the optimality of the design; Roman's coronagraph experience shows hardware dominates.
nodes.signpost: HWO architecture trade documents citing provable throughput bounds; testbed results at 1e-10 broadband with AI-designed masks.

nodes.title: Picometer-stable telescopes with guaranteed control
nodes.description: Wavefront sensing-and-control loops with proven convergence and robustness bounds against thermal and vibration disturbances, co-designed with the error budget, keeping contrast drift below ~1e-11 over hours-long exposures.
nodes.status_oct2026: HWO EAC1 modeling shows significant thermal and vibrational disturbances (JATIS 12(4) 041012, May 2026); segment-level sensing and control studies (JATIS 041024, Jul 2026). Roman launched Aug 30 2026 and took its first coronagraph observation Sep 30 2026 (NASA), the first space demonstration of active wavefront control for high contrast.
nodes.why: Control and estimation with guarantees is applied math (S2 2027-28); proving it works needs vacuum-testbed campaigns and comparison with Roman's in-flight data, which take years and do not compress much (experiment gate).
nodes.strongest_case_small: Control theory is not the bottleneck: metrology, deformable mirrors, detectors and thermal engineering are, and testbed time is scarce.
nodes.signpost: Roman Coronagraph in-flight contrast vs pre-launch models (2026-27); a vacuum-testbed demonstration of HWO-level stability with AI-derived controllers.

nodes.title: HWO's design closed by AI-integrated modeling
nodes.description: End-to-end integrated models (structure, thermal, optics, coronagraph, retrieval, survey yield) run and optimized by AI and used to freeze HWO's aperture, coronagraph type, wavelength range and stability requirements with quantified science yield.
nodes.status_oct2026: HWO is in pre-formulation using Exploratory Analytic Cases (NASA); exposure-time and yield tools exist (pyEDITH, arXiv 2608.28477; EXOSIMS dynamic scheduling, JATIS May 2026); launch in the 2040s (Astro2020, general). NASA FY2026 budget $24.4B; FY2027 request $18.8B (Planetary Society).
nodes.why: Under S2, multiphysics design optimization arrives 2028-29 and can close HWO's requirement tree faster with fewer contractor study cycles. Agency decision points follow budgets, so capital binds; a FY2027 request 23% below FY2026 is a direct threat.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Design closure on paper does not make HWO cheaper to build or launch sooner than the 2040s; agency milestones follow budgets and politics.
nodes.signpost: HWO architecture down-select date and whether it cites AI-run integrated modeling; FY2027 appropriation for HWO.

nodes.title: What space interferometry can prove about black holes
nodes.description: Identifiability and stability theorems for sparse-aperture imaging: which Earth-space baselines (lengths, orientations, frequencies) uniquely determine a black hole's photon-ring diameter and shape, and hence its spin and the Kerr hypothesis, despite unknown plasma emission and station gain errors.
nodes.status_oct2026: Reconstructing images from sparse, corrupted Fourier samples is 'a challenging inverse problem' (ApJ, Jan 2026); BHEX targets the photon ring with the first submillimeter Earth-space VLBI (SPIE, Aug 2026). No catalog family applies: the catalog's inverse-problem results (365, 372) concern elliptic boundary data, not Fourier sampling.
nodes.why: Orbit and baseline choices for a space-VLBI mission are fixed at proposal time; a theorem stating which baseline sets make ring parameters identifiable (and which cannot, a ceiling) can steer a 2026-27 proposal and ngEHT design. Instrument design via inverse-problem theory, acting in 1-2 years.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Mission design already uses simulation-based trade studies; theorems mostly confirm what simulations show, and angular resolution is set by baseline length over wavelength regardless.
nodes.signpost: BHEX or ngEHT design documents citing proven identifiability conditions for baseline selection.

nodes.title: First submillimeter space-VLBI mission flies
nodes.description: A BHEX-class satellite links with ground telescopes to measure a black hole's photon ring, producing the sharpest images in astronomy.
nodes.status_oct2026: BHEX team plans a 2026 NASA Small Explorer proposal and a 2031 launch (blackholeexplorer.org); 4 K cryocooling and antenna designs under development (Cryogenics 2026; SPIE 2024).
nodes.why: Identical across scenarios on purpose: flight needs competitive selection (roughly one-in-several odds, general), a 4-5 year build and a launch slot. AI mathematics improves the proposal, not the selection odds or the build time. Roughly 30% selection times 40% on-time gives about 10-15%, Low.
nodes.strongest_case_small: It is already Low; AI changes nothing measurable here.
nodes.signpost: NASA Small Explorer selection announcement including or excluding BHEX; NASA astrophysics budget for Explorers.

nodes.title: Cosmology inference that knows its own errors
nodes.description: Simulation-based inference, emulators and covariance estimates with proven calibration and error bounds, so Stage-IV surveys (DESI, Euclid, Rubin, Roman) can separate new physics from analysis artefacts with far fewer expensive simulations.
nodes.status_oct2026: Field-level weak-lensing inference with only 60 N-body simulations (Jun 2026); benchmarks of exact, emulated and simulation-based inference (ApJ, Jun 2026); 3x2pt simulation-based pipelines (arXiv 2609.24946, Sep 2026). Catalog 374 (sharp 1/3 stability of optimal-transport maps, T1) bears on error propagation in optimal-transport reconstruction of cosmic initial conditions; catalog 139 (subpolynomial-query log-concave sampling, T3) assumes well-conditioned log-concave targets that real posteriors are not. Both theory-only.
nodes.premise_tier: n/a (catalog links conditional, T1/T3, not load-bearing)
nodes.why: Coverage guarantees and certified emulator errors let collaborations trust neural inference and cut simulation budgets; the gate is collaborations' slow, blinded validation procedures (adoption).
nodes.strongest_case_small: The dominant survey systematics are astrophysical (baryonic feedback, photometric redshifts, intrinsic alignments, shear calibration), not inference mathematics; and collaborations validate pipelines slowly by design.
nodes.signpost: Euclid or Rubin key-project analyses adopting simulation-based inference with formal coverage guarantees.

nodes.title: Is dark energy changing? A decisive answer
nodes.description: Confirmation or refutation, at about 5 sigma, of DESI's hint that dark energy evolves, by combining DESI final data with Euclid, Rubin, Roman and CMB data.
nodes.status_oct2026: DESI DR2 BAO (PRD, 2025) is consistent with DR1; preference for dynamical dark energy does not diminish from DR1 to DR2 (Nature Astronomy, Sep 2025), though some non-parametric reconstructions find reduced support (MNRAS, Dec 2025). Roman launched Aug 30 2026.
nodes.why: Photon-limited: the answer arrives with survey data releases. AI shortens the analysis lag by perhaps a year and lowers the chance a systematic is mistaken for physics; it does not change the answer or bring the data forward.
nodes.strongest_case_small: This is the clearest case where AI mathematics barely matters: same band in all scenarios.
nodes.signpost: Combined DESI final and Euclid DR1 analyses (2027-28).

nodes.title: 3D Sun-to-Earth reconstructions with guarantees
nodes.description: Uniqueness and stability theory, plus certified algorithms, for reconstructing the 3D corona and solar wind (density and magnetic structure) from a few viewpoints and polarized light, a problem now solved with ad hoc regularization.
nodes.status_oct2026: PUNCH (NASA Small Explorer, launched 2025) uses polarization to place structures in 3D (Solar Physics, 2026); discrete polarimetric tomography of CMEs tested on synthetic multi-spacecraft images (Mar 2026); coronal magnetic-field extrapolation from surface data remains ill-posed (general).
nodes.why: Limited-angle tomography has a mature mathematical theory to extend; AI applies it to polarized Thomson scattering and multi-viewpoint geometry, telling forecasters which features are determined by the data and which are prior. Feeds the plasma team's space-weather data-assimilation chain.
nodes.strongest_case_small: With one to three viewpoints the problem is genuinely underdetermined; theory can only say what more data would be needed.
nodes.signpost: Space-weather centers adopting tomographic CME products with stated uncertainty.

nodes.title: Observing constellations designed by inverse-problem theory
nodes.description: Choosing how many spacecraft, where (L1, L4/L5, polar, inner heliosphere) and what they measure, by proving which configurations make the 3D reconstruction unique and stable, instead of choosing by heritage and intuition.
nodes.status_oct2026: Current missions (ESA Vigil at L5, ~2031, general) were designed with conventional trades; no mission concept yet justified by reconstruction-uniqueness analysis (general).
nodes.why: Instrument and constellation design via inverse-problem theory: once uniqueness conditions are known, design optimization can trade spacecraft count against reconstruction error. Adoption happens in concept studies; flight is after 2031.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Launch slots, rideshare availability and budgets decide constellations; Vigil is already designed.
nodes.signpost: A heliophysics mission concept study (multi-point L4/L5/polar) citing reconstruction-uniqueness analysis.

nodes.title: Why the corona is hot: settled
nodes.description: A predictive, data-validated theory of coronal heating and solar-wind acceleration (waves and turbulence versus small-scale reconnection and switchbacks), built by AI from Parker Solar Probe, Solar Orbiter and PUNCH data.
nodes.status_oct2026: Open for about 80 years (general); Parker Solar Probe has made perihelia near 9.9 solar radii since Dec 2024 (general); large data volumes are under-analyzed (general).
nodes.why: One of the few open physics problems where the data largely exist and theory-building is the bottleneck, so S2/S3 physics-theory capability could matter. If settled, it decides what the next heliophysics missions measure (high-cadence spectroscopy versus in-situ kinetic plasma).
nodes.strongest_case_small: Several mechanisms probably operate; 'settled' may mean an energy budget, not one answer; consensus forms slowly and decisive tests may need new in-situ data.
nodes.signpost: An AI-built heating model makes a quantitative prediction confirmed at a later Parker Solar Probe or Solar Orbiter encounter.

nodes.title: Quantum sensors designed against full error budgets
nodes.description: AI-derived systematic-error models (relativistic time transfer, magnetic and gravity-gradient effects, wavefront aberrations) and provably robust quantum-control sequences for space clocks and atom interferometers.
nodes.status_oct2026: ESA's ACES clock ensemble on the ISS since 2025 (ACES payload paper, 2025; relativistic geodesy study using ACES links, arXiv 2609.21786, Sep 2026); differential atom-interferometer magnetometry in NASA's Cold Atom Lab (Nature Communications, Jul 2026); a quantum gravity gradiometer pathfinder is funded (EPJ Quantum Technology, Mar 2025).
nodes.why: Error budgets and robust control are bespoke applied math done by small teams; on-demand AI makes them cheap and complete (P1). Validation needs ground and ISS experiments.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Performance is limited by lasers, vacuum, vibration and atom-source hardware in orbit; error budgets are already well understood by the expert teams.
nodes.signpost: A flight-instrument design review citing AI-derived systematic-error models; ACES or Cold Atom Lab results matching AI-predicted systematics.

nodes.title: AI-co-designed quantum sensor flies
nodes.description: A space atom-interferometer gravity gradiometer or next-generation clock whose design and control were materially derived with AI demonstrates its predicted sensitivity in orbit.
nodes.status_oct2026: Pathfinder funded; no AI-co-designed quantum sensor known to be in flight development (general).
nodes.why: Flight hardware cycles run 4-7 years; a design frozen in 2027-28 flies 2031 at best. Qualification and launch bind in every scenario.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Even S3's faster cognition does not shorten vacuum, vibration and radiation qualification.
nodes.signpost: Quantum gravity gradiometer pathfinder launch date and design methods.

nodes.title: AI mines the space-science archive at scale
nodes.description: AI systems that pose and answer research questions against archival mission data (JWST, Hubble, Gaia, TESS, Fermi, Parker Solar Probe, SDO), building models, running analyses and drafting results, with humans choosing problems and auditing.
nodes.status_oct2026: GPT-5 case studies documented new research steps in physics and astronomy (arXiv 2511.16072, Nov 2025); physicists call for AI verification frameworks before discovery claims (VERaiPHY review, arXiv 2607.10039, Jul 2026).
nodes.why: The capability channel (tl-position-4) with no physical gate: the data are already paid for and public. Most analysis-limited questions in archives are easier than the catalog's problems.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Human verification and refereeing bandwidth (tr-position-5) caps how many results become knowledge, and archival low-hanging fruit is finite.
nodes.signpost: First AI-led discovery in a mission archive confirmed by a follow-up observation; archive-use statistics.

nodes.title: Extraordinary claims audited in weeks
nodes.description: Independent AI re-analyses and certified checks of extraordinary claims (biosignatures, dark-energy anomalies, new-physics hints, exotic-propulsion metrics) published within weeks, with interval-certified or Lean-checked components where possible.
nodes.status_oct2026: Observer-robust energy-condition tests for warp metrics with interval-arithmetic certificates exist (Warpax, arXiv 2602.18023, Feb 2026); the Lentz positive-energy warp claim (2020) was refuted only in Nov 2025 (arXiv 2511.18251); K2-18 b claims were contested over many months (general).
nodes.why: Ceilings and counterexamples act fastest (tl-position-3); a five-year refutation lag shrinks to weeks once outside teams can pose the question. Formal (Lean) checking of GR claims waits on Lorentzian geometry in Mathlib (infra-mathlib-applied).
nodes.strongest_case_small: Contested claims are usually limited by data quality, not analysis speed; faster audits do not settle data-starved questions.
nodes.signpost: A journal or agency formally requiring AI-run independent re-analysis for extraordinary claims.

nodes.title: Lightsails proven to ride the beam
nodes.description: Sail shapes and metasurface designs with proven passive stability under laser propulsion (no tumbling or sliding off the beam) plus thermal and structural margins: the math-and-design half of beamed interstellar-precursor propulsion, the physics-allowed alternative to warp concepts.
nodes.status_oct2026: Beam-riding stability shown in models and early laboratory force measurements (general); no path yet to the ~100 GW-class phased laser arrays a fast interstellar probe needs (general).
nodes.why: Contrast case: here AI mathematics enables (stability proofs, optimized designs) rather than only bounding. The design is cognitive and lands early; everything after it is capital and hardware.
nodes.strongest_case_small: The binding constraints are the laser array (capital, power, phasing) and sail materials, not stability theory.
nodes.signpost: Laboratory demonstration of self-stabilizing laser propulsion of a sail-like membrane.

nodes.title: Laser-propelled sail demonstrated
nodes.description: Ground or orbital demonstration of stable laser-driven propulsion of a gram-scale or smaller sail.
nodes.status_oct2026: No funded flight demonstration (general).
nodes.why: Funding and laser hardware bind; only S3's broader economic effects make an early demonstration plausible.
nodes.strongest_case_small: No sponsor, no demo, whatever the mathematics.
nodes.signpost: A funded program for a high-power laser propulsion demonstration.

nodes.title: No-go theorems redirect breakthrough-propulsion money
nodes.description: Sharp, audited no-go results move the small pool of breakthrough-propulsion funding and attention away from warp and reactionless concepts toward physics-allowed frontiers (fusion, beamed sails).
nodes.status_oct2026: NASA's Breakthrough Propulsion Physics Project (1996-2002) reported six of 14 tasks reaching null conclusions (NTRS 20060000022) and about a third of 16 tasks not viable (NTRS 20040070788); warp research continues to be published (e.g., atmospheric-signature study of zero-ADM-mass warp bubbles, arXiv 2608.10800, Aug 2026).
nodes.premise_tier: T5 for the core no-go theorems
nodes.why: Ceilings change what people stop doing (fc-position-1 exception). Program managers and investors can cite an audited theorem instead of a debate. Medium in every scenario because the gate is human belief, not mathematics.
nodes.strongest_case_small: The dollars at stake are tiny (single-digit millions per year, general) and the most committed proponents rarely respond to theorems; the ceilings were mostly known by 2021.
nodes.signpost: Funding calls (NIAC, private institutes) explicitly excluding concepts that require energy-condition violation.

nodes.title: More science per mission dollar
nodes.description: With analysis, theory and modeling nearly free, the science extracted from each flown observatory rises sharply; photons, downlink and mission count become the bottleneck of space science.
nodes.status_oct2026: Archives of JWST, Hubble, Gaia, TESS and heliophysics missions are public and under-analyzed (general); budget pressure is rising (NASA FY2027 request $18.8B vs $24.4B FY2026).
nodes.why: The main 2031 outcome in this domain. The cognitive clock compresses analysis of data already paid for; nothing physical gates it until the archives are exhausted, after which new photons bind.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Paper counts are not discoveries; referee bandwidth limits absorption; budget cuts may remove missions faster than AI raises yield per mission.
nodes.signpost: Discoveries from archival data per year; agency reports on archive science yield.

nodes.title: Space science shifts money from analysis to photons
nodes.description: Agencies and decadal surveys rebalance toward more data-collecting missions (small satellites, rideshares, probes) and laboratory data, because AI makes analysis and theory cheap.
nodes.status_oct2026: Priorities set by decadal surveys (Astro2020; the next astrophysics survey is expected around 2030-31, general).
nodes.why: If cognition is near-free, the marginal dollar buys more science as data than as analysis. Agencies act through budget cycles and decadal surveys, so the effect appears at the next survey at the earliest.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Budgets are set by politics, and flagship commitments (HWO, the LISA contribution) lock in spending for a decade.
nodes.signpost: Terms of reference for the next astrophysics decadal survey addressing AI analysis capacity.

scenario_contrast: S1 (plateau): research-grade AI mathematics reaches outside teams around 2027-28 but stays strongest in pure mathematics; the domain gets fast ceilings (warp no-go theorems, coronagraph and interferometry identifiability limits, claim audits) and an archival-analysis boost, while LISA's self-force program, LISA-grade numerical relativity and biosignature theory finish on roughly their pre-AI schedules (after 2031). S2 (exponential, base case): applied math is routine by 2027-28 and physics theory by 2028-29, so the expert-scarce theory backlog collapses: second-order self-force in Kerr by ~2029 (four to six years early), LISA analysis readiness by ~2030, retrieval identifiability and certified cosmological inference by 2028, quantified biosignature false-positive maps by ~2030 and AI-closed HWO requirements by ~2030. Yet no flight date moves: LISA still launches in 2035, HWO in the 2040s, BHEX no earlier than 2031, and dark-energy and biosignature questions wait for photons. S3 (recursive) pulls the cognitive nodes forward another year and raises bands on theory-heavy items (beyond-GR well-posedness, coronal heating), but compute (numerical relativity), laboratory validation (opacities), qualification (quantum sensors) and capital (BHEX, HWO, lightsail demos) bind just as hard. The domain's signature is a widening gap between theory readiness and data arrival: by 2031 under S2, space science is limited by photons, downlink and budgets rather than by analysis.
key_insights: In space science AI mathematics changes the cognitive half of a mission (theory, waveforms, inference, design closure) and none of the flight dates: LISA 2035, HWO 2040s and BHEX no earlier than 2031 in every scenario.

The highest-leverage targets are expert-scarce applied problems, not famous conjectures: second-order self-force around spinning black holes is done today only for circular orbits around non-spinning ones; under S2 it could finish around 2029, four to six years ahead of the pre-AI path, turning LISA's extreme-mass-ratio science from a risk into a baseline.

The catalog's GR results are science-only. Family 264 (strong cosmic censorship near Kerr) has zero mission relevance; family 260 (spacetime Penrose inequalities) is T1 for its main inequalities. Only a supporting construction has unchecked Lean, and the repo's own Lean doc says the general inequality is unformalized. Both raise confidence (P5); neither changes a model.

For exotic propulsion AI mathematics can only deliver ceilings, and the ceilings were mostly in place before AI: the null-energy theorem (2021) and positive mass (1979-81). What is new is sharpness and auditing at scale: the Sep 2026 Natario result shows negative energy grows as R^4/Delta^3, so halving a bubble wall costs 8x more. The effect is to redirect a tiny funding pool, not to enable anything.

Where AI mathematics enables in this domain, it does so through inverse-problem theory feeding instrument design: coronagraph throughput limits, space-VLBI identifiability, heliospheric tomography uniqueness, quantum-sensor error budgets. These act within 1-3 years (P3/P5) and inform designs frozen in 2027-30, but fly after 2031.

Data-bound questions (is dark energy evolving, is a gas biological, Hubble tension) are not settled by mathematics; AI shortens analysis lag by about a year and makes claims more credible, but photons bind.

The main 2031 outcome is more science per mission dollar from public archives, a High-band effect in S2 because nothing physical gates it, set against a NASA budget request 23% lower for FY2027 than FY2026's enacted level.

General relativity is a formalization desert: Mathlib has essentially no Lorentzian geometry, so GR results will stay at T1-T3 longer than discrete mathematics, and certified warp-drive audits will rely on interval arithmetic before Lean.
nil_effects: Launch and flight dates: LISA (2035), HWO (2040s) and BHEX (2031 at earliest) do not move in any scenario; capital, fabrication, qualification and launch bind.
No warp drive, reactionless drive or traversable wormhole becomes possible; AI mathematics can only tighten no-go bounds (ceilings, P3).
Strong cosmic censorship near Kerr (264) has no mission or engineering implication.
Photon-limited questions (5-sigma dark-energy evolution, Hubble tension, a biosignature on a specific planet) are gated by survey and telescope data, not mathematics.

The galactic matrix-multiplication and FFT bounds in the release do not speed up cosmology, gravitational-wave or imaging pipelines (tl-position-1); log-concave sampling (139) is theory-only for real multimodal posteriors.
Angular resolution of space VLBI is set by baseline length over wavelength and coronagraph contrast by diffraction, wavefront stability and photon noise; theorems define limits, not new physics.
Quantum-sensor sensitivity in orbit is hardware-limited (lasers, vacuum, atom sources); laboratory spectroscopy, vacuum testbeds and supercomputer time do not compress with cognition.
The catalog's elliptic inverse-problem results (365, 372) do not apply to Fourier-sampled interferometric imaging or line-of-sight tomography.

signposts.what_it_changes: Moves science-gr-foundations from T1 to T2 or higher; a scope gap in 260 would also remove its marginal extension of warp mass bounds.

signposts.what_it_changes: Confirms S2 timing for science-second-order-self-force (2029) and science-lisa-readiness (2030); no such result by 2029 means S1 timing.

signposts.what_it_changes: Starts the P1 clock for all tier-2 nodes; a delay pushes S2 dates back roughly one-for-one.

tables.title: Ceilings versus enablement: what AI mathematics can do in each area
rows: Sharp no-go theorems (null-energy violation, negative-energy minima scaling as R^4/Delta^3, positive-mass and Penrose mass bounds); certified audits of proposed metrics
Quantum energy inequalities in curved or interacting settings
Strong cosmic censorship near Kerr (264, T1)
Second-order self-force in Kerr; precision numerical relativity with error control
Coronagraph throughput limits, controllers with guarantees, retrieval identifiability, false-positive theory
Both: limits prune architectures; designs and theory enable
Identifiability of photon-ring parameters from sparse baselines
Enablement of design, plus a ceiling on what is measurable
Uniqueness and stability of 3D tomography; constellation design; heating theory
Enablement of analysis; no answer without data
